correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the backward Poisson ODE and two endpoint conditions; Kirchhoff balance gives A/(DB) for arbitrary positive lengths and any nonnegative budget simplex. Strict convexity of A-VB at the optimum yields uniqueness. Interior KKT and the universal A>=sum(length)/2, B<=sum(rate) bound exclude lambda>=V and hence all inactive terminals. Exact formulas have correct units; positivity of B guarantees finiteness. Independent derivative algebra and 210 randomized global minimizations with 2520 additional feasible competitors support, but do not replace, the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A natural heterogeneous network capture-design problem asks whether finite reactivity can optimally be omitted from a distant/short terminal. The theorem gives a global negative answer for every finite budget, regardless of geometry, and uniquely characterizes the full continuous allocation via scalar equations. It is a structural theorem for arbitrary branching degree and unequal lengths, not a tiny numerical gain, isolated example or known-table recomputation. Applicability is deliberately limited to central launch and compact metric stars.
